utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Jadranko Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. On this Tuesday, 17th of March, 2009, I greet the counsels, particularly Ms. Nozica. I greet Mr. Stringer and his colleagues. And I do not forget to greet all of those who have -- who are assisting us, Mr. Registrar, Mr. Usher, and as soon as the witness has his headphones on, Your Excellency, I greet you, for the ordnance of today. First of all, I'll give the floor to the Registrar who has two IC numbers to give us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. 2D has submitted its objections to Prosecution's list of documents tendered through witness Hamid Bahto. It has also submitted its response to Prosecution's objections to its documents tendered through Tihomir Majic. These lists shall be given number IC952 and IC953 respectively. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you Mr. Registrar. The Trial Chamber is going to hand out an oral decision. As you know, the Defence team for General Petkovic requested additional time. The Trial Chamber invited General Petkovic's Defence team to send us, during the night, its written submission, which we have received this morning. The request is entitled "confidential and ex parte." The Trial Chamber deliberated this morning before coming into court and feels that there is no need to listen to the position of other Defence teams or that of the Prosecution regarding the allocation of time which was indicated in the guide-lines. The Trial Chamber feels that given the guide-lines in practice, the Chamber gives 50 per cent of the time to the other Defence teams when a witness via the request of the Prosecution. It is possible that under very exceptional circumstances, the Trial Chamber proves flexible and changes this allocation of time. The Trial Chamber wants to remind everyone that it is up to every single party to put the matter before us long in advance when it has been given the summaries for the requests for additional time so that the Trial Chamber can scrutinize the requests and hand out decisions in the matter. The Trial Chamber indicates that in this particular case, the matter was put before it belatedly, first of all orally yesterday and this was confirmed by a written submission yesterday. Exceptionally, the Trial Chamber has decided to examine the merits of this request and to make a decision on this request. Having scrutinized the request and having looked at the arguments presented, the Trial Chamber feels that it is reasonable to allocate two hours to General Petkovic's Defence team. This same Defence team having requested two and a half hours. The Trial Chamber also allocates other Defence teams with a general time of one hour. So we had allocated one and a half hours, we have now moved on to three hours. Ms. Nozica, you have the floor and you can carry on with your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, before we move to my learned leader, I will for the record say that I am of course respecting the decision of the Trial Chamber, somewhat perplexed on the face of it that whilst this matter was raised yesterday, there was no indication whatsoever that an ex parte confidential motion was going to be filed by my learned friend. And in fact, she had told me that -- my understanding was that we were going to receive this document at 5.00. Now, we've been waiting for that motion and been looking for this motion, and it would have been very helpful if we had been informed, as a matter of courtesy if nothing else, that an ex parte confidential motion was being filed so we didn't have to waste our time and wait in vein for a motion that we are not going to receive. That's the first point of. Your Honour, the second issue is that it seems, again on the face it, somewhat unusual that an ex parte confidential motion for an extension of time has been filed, and Your Honours have considered that without the benefit of any submissions. Your Honours, of course I'm not privy to the actual contents. I'm sure that Your Honours in reviewing the motion would have given the most anxious scrutiny as to whether or not that motion merited being withheld from the other parties to litigation and to allow us a chance to respond to that motion. Your Honours, I can't go behind a motion which has been denied us -- that we have been denied sight of. So all I can say for the record is that I do trust that Your Honours will have given the anxious scrutiny to whether or not it merited an ex parte confidential filing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may be heard very briefly, Your Honour, because I would depart with my learned friend's comments. I don't think, when it comes to cross-examination because that's what we are speaking of, whether it's the Prosecution or another Defence team, that one has to show and share their hand in advance. This is a common technique and I commend my colleague for having the foresight of doing that. I would have done the same thing, so I don't think that anybody is disadvantaged at that. And I think that that would be the better practice in the future. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, may I just thank you for the time allocated to me and my -- thank my colleague, Mr. Karnavas, who is well known in this courtroom as a person who teaches others as to how witnesses should be examined, so he gave a professional explanation of how all this should be dealt with. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President and Your Honours. Ms. Alaburic did give me the courtesy of informing me before trial that before the proceedings began this morning than an ex parte filing had been made. I accepted the fact that it was made ex parte because she didn't have an obligation to disclose to other parties the reasons behind why she needed more time. So in that respect, I tend to align myself more with the position advanced by Mr. Karnavas, that it was appropriate under the circumstances. Having said that, can I just propose that we get on with the examination of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Nozica, we are not going to waste any time on this because I hope that everyone will be in a position to ask questions to the witness. So Ms. Nozica, you have one hour and 30 minutes left, so please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I wish to greet everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bandic. I would like to ask you to look at the second binder. I don't know if you have the documents there with you. The second binder, please. We have come to document P5226. Have you found the document?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bandic, this is a document dated the 20th of September, 1993. It was submitted by the assistant head to Mate Boban, the president of the HZ-HB, and in this letter he writes about an incident that was caused by members of the Convicts Battalion on the 17th of September, 1993, in Ljubuski. Unfortunately, we don't have the document that is mentioned in the letter, but I would like to ask you whether you remember what kind of incident this was and why it was necessary to send this kind of request to Mr. Boban?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, I am quite familiar with this incident. It was a very serious one. The members of the Convicts Battalion in a way took justice in their own hands, and they took away a member of the HVO who was killed then, as was later established. This was an incident that threatened to bring about an escalation of the conflict in the HVO, so that's why Mr. Lucic wrote directly to Mr. Boban.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Tell me, as far as the Convicts Battalion is concerned, and Mr. Mate Boban, did you have any knowledge about the relations between the Convicts Battalion and Mate Boban and can you give us your comments, were those the reasons why Mr. Lucic directly addressed Mate Boban?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was basically a generally known thing that the top authority over these units, in this case the Convicts Battalion, was exercised by Mr. Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please let us look at the next document, 2D925. Could we please have a look at that now. This is a document signed by Mladen Naletilic Tuta. He sends this to President Boban, and he says, "Two of our captains are working at the SIS," the mentioned persons there, and then he is asking Mr. Boban to sign the ranks for these persons. What is important is that Mr. Naletilic is signing this letter as the personal advisor to Mr. Boban. Did you know that that is the way he introduced himself and that he was that in a way? Do you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam Lawyer, this is, of course, an unusual relationship between Mr. Boban and Mr. Naletilic. Of course, I know that he introduced himself as the personal advisor or as the General or simply as Tuta. However, it is an interesting document because I know both of the persons on this list. I know that they were sent from the Convicts Battalion to be SIS officers in the administration or at the Mostar centre of SIS.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yesterday we started discussing reports and communication between the administration of the SIS, the centres of the SIS, and SIS officers in units, so I'd like to ask you to look at the next document, is P5614. This is a request, if we can put it that way. It was sent to Mr. Lucic, it was sent by Mr. Petkovic to check some information, some incidents that had happened. First of all, I'd like to ask you whether you knew of the existence of this request, and did you know what this was all about?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of this request. In this case, Mr. Petkovic is asking for information from the SIS administration. There were several such cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could we please look at the next document, that is 2D940. This is Mr. Lucic's response to the previous request. Mr. Lucic is providing information about each and every point made in this request, and finally I'd like to draw your attention to this, perhaps it has to do with you. The last sentence in this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's one tiny little problem I have about victims. I see on this document that the rape of a lady is mentioned. Shouldn't this document be in closed session? You know, I'm just stepping in the victim's shoes here who possibly wouldn't want to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do agree with you. I would just like to mention that the document is an Exhibit, so it has been used in this courtroom, but of course I don't mind. On the contrary, this document and the next document, the next document also contains names, and I don't mind both documents being handled in this way, and I think this is fully in accordance with the rule that no victims should be exposed to any kind of unpleasantness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Could I be shown the name of the woman? Where is the name of the victim mentioned in the document? I'm looking at P05614. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It's in the next document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Oh, I'm awfully sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- Your Honour, 940.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm awfully sorry, I was mistaken. I withdraw everything, apologise, and shut up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, the most important thing here is for this document not to be shown outside the courtroom, but of course you can refer to the document. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The last sentence of this document could pertain to you. It says: "More detailed information can be obtained from our officers who are operating within the GS, the Main Staff." Did that pertain to you, Mr. Bandic? The 8th of October, 1993 is the date of this document. By then were you an officer at the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a compiled report, and the second part I think it was me, physically. Perhaps it was another gentleman. If necessary I can give you his name, Predrag Covic. I'm not sure if it was him or me, but I think that I was up there then.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you say "up there" what do you mean, Mr. Bandic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, usually I mean that physically, the Main Staff. I think that at that moment it was in Citluk.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'd now like us to look at document 2D1495. This is a report. 2D1495, yes, we have the right number. It is a report from the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade. We see that it's signed by the assistant commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, and he is submitting this to the assistant of the commander for security of central Bosnia, Ante Sliskovic. I would just like this to show what the mode of communication was as far as his officers in the units were concerned and who they sent these reports to. Now, this way of communication where the assistant commander of the brigade for SIS sends his report. As we can see, he is sending it the assistant commander for security of the OZ. We are talking about central Bosnia, right? Could you clarify the matter by using this document? Can you explain what the communication was?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam lawyer, Your Honours, this document should be the pattern that demonstrates how communication functioned between the SIS in units all the way up to the operative zone because this operative zone was the top operative body as far as the security service was concerned, and this military security aspect.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at the next document, P2597. It's an exhibit, so we don't have to give any comments on the content. We are just dealing with the form.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The date is the 1st of June, 1993. Rama Prozor Brigade, the Security Information Service. Down here it says SIS officer where the signature is, and it's submitted to the SIS of the operative zone and the commander of the Rama Brigade. Can you give us your comments. Was this the right way to proceed, to send these reports by these desk officers? We have a desk officer here. We do not have an assistant commander. Is this the right way to proceed and to communicate?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am personally -- I know Mr. Krizanac personally, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: For the transcript, what did you say about the way the communication? Here it says, "Yes, I know the gentleman personally." Is this the desirable way to communicate, if I can put it that way, as envisaged by the rules?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Precisely. That is what I wished to confirm. This is the way in which there was communication at the desired level and on the basis of the regulations. This is what was aspired for and that is what the rules say.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you please look at the next document, that is P3260.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I didn't want to ask you these questions because we have little time, but I must ask you the question. We see a report from the Rama Brigade SIS, and we see that it relates to an event which they were made aware of by the observers of the European community, so the report has been written. And I assume - could you please confirm this - I assume that this report will then be sent to the commander of the Rama Brigade, who in turn having received the report probably will request from the military police to investigate and will then put the matter before the Prosecutor in order for proceedings to be introduced. Is that the way it should occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is the right way to proceed. I'm sure of that. In this specific case, I don't know what was done after this, but the SIS of the brigade familiarized the commander of the brigade, and that is their basic task, and also then the SIS of the operative zone. That is the right way to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you, can we continue. The next document is P3260. This is a report. It says SIS division. It's signed by the commander -- assistant commander of the operative zone, and it has to do with the security of eastern Herzegovina. It's submitted to the commander of the operative zone, and the assistant head for security. Is that the third link when a report is compiled by security assistants in the operative zone?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. Once again, I confirm that that is from an operative and military point of view, that was the chain. The assistant commander of the operative zone for SIS was the last link in this chain of the military operative chain, and the activity of SIS through units. And then that part goes towards the centre that is professionally in charge. If you allow me, in this particular case it has to do with the Mostar centre. Out of all the centres, it was the one that was at the level that we really desired, or rather, wanted to have envisaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This report is sent at the same time to the commander of the operative zone; isn't that right? We see that down here as in cc'd?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That is a primary matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: P6555. It is signed by Mladen Zovko Kuhar. Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber whether you know this person, and did he have a post in the Stepjan Turija Battalion?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know this person, Mladen Zovko, he was a man in from the SIS in the independent battalion Herceg-Stepjan. But in addition to that, this is a document that is interesting in terms of who Mr. Zovko is addressing. These were very delicate developments in the area at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As we can see from this document, it is proposed here -- as Mr. Zovko says, what is proposed is an exchange of territories or, rather, a handover of territories for money. Fahrudin Fazlic, Mr. Seljdic [phoen], those are the names that are mentioned. Mr. Bandic, was that the reason, that's what I wanted to ask you, why this kind of report from the SIS is being submitted to Mr. Stojic, Mr. Petkovic, Mr. Lucic, and Mr. Keza. That was an exception from the rule, wasn't it, in terms of the hierarchy, how reports were being sent. Is that because of the content of the document?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I mentioned, that this situation was an exceptional one. Although, there are going to be other situations where this chain would not be observed as appropriate, but indeed this was an exceptionally delicate situation. And that is why Mr. Zovko, as I've already said, acted this way. He was the SIS officer in the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we are going to change subjects. I just need a brief explanation. Please look at document P7035. This document is an exhibit. We've used it more than once in the courtroom. It is a compilation of information concerning events of crimes on the territory of the HZ-HB. It covers a rather long period and almost the entire territory. The crimes are listed both by kind of crime, type of crime, and the area where it was committed. But, please, could you clarify to the Chamber why Mr. Lucic was submitting this report to the attention of Mr. Miroslav Tudjman and to the HIS, so why was this sent to another state, another service, and could you please explain to the Court what this service was and what it dealt with, if you know, at that time?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am familiar with this information. I know that this is a compilation which was made in late 1993. My explanation of this document is the following: Many crimes were committed, as is evident from this document, there were many perpetrators who practically moved back and forth across the border which was quite porous. This was away of attempting to establish cooperation on both sides of the border in order to attempt to prevent such crimes. That is my interpretation of this document. Another interpretation, in my view, because this was a time when negotiations were already beginning, the negotiations which culminated in the Washington Agreement, and the end of the war between the army of BH and the HVO, so it seems logical it to me that -- an overview, a summary should be made of crimes which had taken place in order to clearly define things. So this was an attempt to communicate and establish cooperation. As for your third question, counsel, as regards the work of the Croatian intelligence service, the HIS, if it's relevant for this case I would ask the Court to speak about this in closed session or private session because I'm not authorised to discuss this.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bandic, there's no need. I just wanted to ask whether one could say in general that this service dealt in such matters. I don't want to delve into it any further.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Nozica. Mr. Bandic, I would be grateful if you would elaborate and explain a bit the answer you have given. I have, of course, not been able in the short time to read this lengthy, lengthy document which has 24 pages. I have not found anything in it, by looking through it, which indicates that it has anything to do with cooperation. There's no reference to that. There's no frame about it. And I also do not see the logic which would link this to the negotiations for the Washington Agreement. Maybe you could explain it and clarify this for me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Your Honour, I'll do my best. I wish to mention that crossing the border between Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Republic of Croatia at that time, was something that was difficult to control, something that happened very frequently, and it was quite possible for perpetrators of various crimes to cross the border very easily. That, I believe, is the basis for this correspondence. You will have observed that there are very many people mentioned here. At the time those people had dual nationality. It was very simple for them to cross the border. Also, Your Honour, there were persons who were able to continue their activities within the military or the political arena. That is my own perception. I believe it was very important to have information which was as detailed as possible about everything that had been happening, especially all things that had the characteristics of a crime or an illegal activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I will not insist on further. Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In connection with His Honour's question, could you please look at the front page of this document, the last name there, it says against Daris Kapovic Klokan, a member of the HV from Zadar. A warrant has been issued for his arrest because there are grounds to suspect that he committed theft. That he stole personal property and weapons of HVO officers who had been killed. Is this something that corroborates your opinion that that was an important reason to establish cooperation in view of the fact that members of both the HV and the HVO could move about freely on both territories so that appropriate action could be taken?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't go into details, although I'm quite familiar with many of these details, and this is an illustrative example. Let me add the following hypothetical situation: If a brigade commander was duty-bound to act on this information, then he would not -- he should not have been allowed to continue his activities after the war ended.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bandic, I'll move on to a topic now which we might describe as the information and actions of the SIS having to do with military prisons and places where prisoners were kept. Please look at the first document having to do with this topic, that's P4756. What I wish to show you is on page 3 in the Croatian text and on page 4 in the English text. Yesterday, I asked you whether you had attended this meeting of the collegium and you said you hadn't, but I wished to ask you whether you are familiar with some of the activities that the SIS undertook in connection with the conclusions reached by this collegium. It says what military prisons existed in the HZ-HB, and after a discussion, the decision was made to visit all places where prisoners of war were kept and to establish precisely, as Mr. Lucic said, who was behind these prisons, who was doing these things, and to what extent certain measures could be taken. That's exactly what was said. A conclusion was reached. Mr. Bandic, are you aware that members of the SIS administration or SIS centre acted on this conclusion and compiled information on Heliodrom, Ljubuski, Gabela, and Dretelj as listed here?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this document in detail. I never attended meetings of the collegium, but I do know that attempts were made - as can be seen from this document also - to draw up a definite list of these prisons, to record them, to make a sort of inventory, and to find out what legal grounds there were for further detention because evidently there was chaos prevailing in all this.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please look at P5133. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a request dated the 16th of September, after this collegium as we can see, and it was addressed to the military prisons in Dretelj and Gabela to the attention of Mr. Tomo Sakota, and operatives of the SIS in Mostar, Mr. Predrag Covic and Mr. Dragan-Zdenko Maric, are to be given full access to the prison. Was it the practice for SIS operatives to enter any prison, whether military prison or prison where prisoners of war were kept, only pursuant to a request such as this one? Was this the practice?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was how things were done.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please tell me, are you familiar with the name of Tomo Sakota, and did you know who this person was at the time when this request was sent?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know Mr. Sakota personally, unfortunately he is deceased.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know what duty he performed at that time when this request was submitted for his visit to the Dretelj and Gabela camps or prisons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what his title was. I think he was either the warden or the coordinator of both prisons.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please look at P7 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm trying to understand all of this, the prisons of a military nature or of a civilian nature. This seems very confusing according to all the documents we have. Let's get back to the previous document. Clearly, Mr. Stojic states that there are two military prisons, Ljubuski and the Heliodrom, and that there are other prisons, Gabela and Dretelj, in which detainees are held, but he adds, I don't feel that these are military prisons, and he will not take on the work carried out in these prisons. This is the last document which stems from SIS and is addressed to Gabela and Dretelj that are qualified as military prisons. So I don't understand anything at all. According to you, Gabela and Dretelj, are these prisons military prisons or prisons for civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, to the best of my knowledge, Dretelj and Gabela were for a while military prisons also in one period of time. But I do know that later on there were also civilians there. As far as I know, there was never a clear distinction made as to what were prison, what were collection centres, and it was never fully clear to me either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bandic, let's go back a little bit. Regardless of what Mr. Lucic called these two prison, let's go back to this document which is from the collegium, and it's a number 4756. Is it clear from these minutes, does it follow from these minutes, where the head of the department said, We have two military prisons, the Heliodrom and the military prison in Ljubuski. Was this beyond doubt the position in the Defence Department as regards those two prisons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President to the leading question. Counsel is trying to take the witness to a specific place that the witness has not indicated is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Ms. Nozica, please rephrase your question. Your question was extremely leading.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem, Your Honour. I was only relying on what you read out to the witness. I put the same question to the witness, does this follow from these minutes, but now I'll put my question very precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What was the position of the Defence Department and the SIS as regards the existence of military prisons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, as for the Heliodrom prison and the Ljubuski prison, they were considered to be military prisons. What I was saying here was that it was never fully clear to me what the status of the prisons in Dretelj and Gabela was and, once again, Grabovina, where I was personally when the Neum case took place. I don't know what the status of that prison was either, and the persons connected to the Neum case were brought there, the one we talked about yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you mention that prison, were those persons we talked about yesterday brought in there and were they civilians?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, what prison are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The one in Grabovina that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could we now take a look at document P7341.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Ms. Nozica, if I may come back to the document. Mr. Bandic, I would invite you to go one page further, the next page, at least it's the next page in the English version. There is a passage at the end of item 3 which is underlined. In English it starts reading: "The SIS, the military police administration, and the Health Sector shall draft separate reports on the work of the Dretelj and Gabela prisons..." and so forth. Do you attribute any significance to that passage with regard of the question previously addressed; namely, that these two prisons are completely outside of the field and of the area of competence of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my understanding was the following: An attempt was made to register this, to record it as regards health simply to assess the situation of the people who were there as regards their physical and mental health, and for the SIS to look at who was there from the security aspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Who took this conclusion? Was this a conclusion in which the head of the Defence Department concurred? Was he also one who stood behind this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I presume that this was so. I do not know who attended the collegiums meeting, but I believe that this would be a logical path to take.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I asked the document 7341, P7341 to be brought up. We discussed Mr. Sakota, so let's continue with that. This is a report on the work of the coordinator for inmates and prisoners of war in the territory of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, for the period between 22nd July 1993 and 25th of December, 1993. It is signed by Mr. Tomo Sakota. Mr. Bandic, did you have knowledge that Mr. Sakota dealt with these issues and that he had been appointed by the president of HZ-HB to assume that position?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was known to me because I personally knew Mr. Sakota, the late Mr. Sakota. I remember that this was at a time of intensive talks and negotiations about the release of inmates, and I know that Mr. Sakota played an important role at the time. And I think if it's pertinent, after that he became a member of staff of the general consulate of Republic of Croatia in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's take a look at the next document, 2D973. This is a request by Mr. Sakota, dated 1995 to the ministry of foreign affairs of the Republic of Croatia. In the third paragraph Mr. Sakota says: "I was a member of the military police only for me in 1993, for Mr. Mate Boban to ask me to take up the post of the warden of the Dretelj collection centre. Soon after that I was appointed warden of all the collection centres in the HZ-HB." Does this confirm what you just said, Mr. Bandic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly that. I think that at the time Mr. Sakota's role was very sensitive and very positive and this was the reason why he later was appointed to this position, and I would meet him on several occasions in the consulate general of the Republic of Croatia in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you say that position, you mean the position at the consulate general, am I right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Fine. Let's take a look at the next document. We are dealing with the same topic, that's 2D926. We saw what was the conclusion of the collegium about the drafting of reports. If you know, please confirm whether this document submits those information to the president of HZ-HB, the information concerning this information in the operation zone south-east Herzegovina. Do you know whether the president received that information?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not familiar with the individual documents out of those four, but I do know that the president was informed of that. This was one of the ways of reporting, particularly in delicate situations such, as this one was, whenever the need arose to take this path given that this pertained to very delicate events and developments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, one moment, please. Ivica Lucic addresses himself directly to the president, Mr. Boban, without referring to his superior. To do so, it's as if an ambassador addresses himself directly to the president without referring to the minister of foreign affair. Was this customary? Was this how things operated at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the situation necessitated, obviously, to communicate in this way, although this was not the ordinary way of doing things. You compare this with the situation of an ambassador and the ministry of foreign affairs and president, but this is valid in well ordered states in times of calm, but this situation was extremely difficult. If you allow me, I would like to emphasise that Mr. Lucic assessed at the time that the authority of Mr. Boban was the greatest and that his influence would be the decisive factor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's take a look at the next document, 2D950, dealing with the same topic. Discusses a request on the -- based on the verbal agreement with Mr. Kraljevic, head of military investigation, detention, Ljubuski, and Mr. Sesar. For you to allow Mr. Stanko Juric, coordinator from SIS administration, to visit Mr. Franjo Brajko and talk to him. Mr. Bandic, Franjo Brajko seems to a Croatian person who was in VIZ Ljubuski, and this was a military prison in Ljubuski. Would this be an ordinary request? Whenever SIS operatives would talk to somebody in detention centre, would such a request be a prerequisite for them doing so?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the standard operating procedure as per regulations, and I believe that this was adhered to.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now the last document, 2D929, dealing with this topic. That is addressed to the Heliodrom, Mr. Bosic, the warden. What is requested is an interview with Suad Repko and Milorad Tribun signed by the head of the SIS centre of Mostar, isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was the regular path, ordinary procedure to be followed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to ask to go into private session for a general ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are now in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bandic, let's take a look at the document, it's a report or two reports in succession. The first one is P561 -- 5619 [as interpreted]. STRINGER: Excuse me, is that 5619 or 6519?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, P6519. Well, P in Croatian is homonymous with 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Have you seen this document, Mr. Bandic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you draft this report, first of all? Did you draft it? You read it, this is an exhibit, there's no need for us to dwell much on it. We do not have much time, but briefly I'm going to ask you whether you drafted it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never drafted it and I've never seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So you answered my third question there. The second was supposed to be, did you take any part in any way in drafting this report?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said that you've never seen it. I'd like to know whether you know the gist or the contents of this report and the details contained therein?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Details were not known to me, but I do know the circumstances and I know of that event.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: At the end of the report it says that it was submitted to SIS, whatever that may mean, whether it's an SIS of a brigade or operation zone or operations group, et cetera. Could you confirm to the Chamber whether the SIS administration at Mostar ever received this report?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not familiar with this, and I don't know whether this document ever reached the SIS at Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, let's take a look at P6671. Mr. Bandic, my questions are the same, whether you drafted this report, whether you did take part in the drafting of this document, and whether you've ever seen this report?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer to all those three questions is no.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bandic, could you take a look at 2D574. Here we can see that on the 28th of October, 1993, the deputy of a district military Prosecutor did take some activities to detect possible criminal offences or perpetrators in connection with the Stupni Do situation. When did you learn that the Prosecutor was doing these things?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately one month after this date towards the end of November, and this date is 28th of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We have another document concerning the investigation, it's 2D578, dated the 19th of December, 1993. Here we can see that this document confirms that activities had -- that had been started were continuing. You knew at the end of November that the Prosecutor had undertaken certain actions?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, something in November and during December some things were done. It was known to me that the military Prosecutor had undertaken action.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now let's take a look at the document 6137. It is an order signed by Mr. Petkovic addressed to Mr. Rajic. It is an order for the undertaking of an investigation in the Stupni Do incident. Mr. Bandic, did you see that order or this order at that time or at a later date?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen this order until now that I've become a witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bandic, pursuant to the document that we saw here, you attended two meetings at the Main Staff of the UN protection force at Kiseljak. I will show you a document, P6049, which predates those meetings. P6049. Mr. Vinko Lucic signs this as a liaison officer with the UN. Could you please explain who Mr. Vinko Lucic was, whether you knew him, what were his tasks?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I personally know Mr. Lucic. He was a liaison officer, which means the official representative of the Croatian Defence Council for contacts with international community organisations, UNPROFOR. I know him quite well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's take a look at document P6963. It is a voluminous document. Towards the end of your binder it's a report of the UNPROFOR. And when you reach the Croatian translation, only the first two pages in the English version refer to the meeting that you had. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: There is mention on the 22nd of November that there was a meeting with Colonel Lucic, investigator from the Main Staff of the HVO Mostar, Mr. Bandic. They wanted to assist concerning the investigation of the incident at Stupni Do, the HVO was ready to cooperate. Could you please explain this item 2 -- well, you can explain the whole report, whether it reflects developments as you remember them. What I'm interested in is item 2 where Mr. Bandic introduced himself after me, that would be 6963. No, this is a document under seal, I've just received information that this document is under seal. I apologise. Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, is the document under seal, because if it is then it will need be to redacted? We'll move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have five minutes to the break right? Am I right? Yes. I'll continue for these five minutes. P6647. Could we have a look at that, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bandic, this document is an exhibit. We are familiar with it, we in this courtroom. It is called, "Combined Operation Kiseljak, Information of Interest to Security." I'm not going to go into the content of the document. The 13th of November, 1993, is the number [as interpreted] of this document. And now I'd like to look at P6828. P6828. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a document provided by Mr. Biskic, and we see who he is sending this to. It says, I am providing information to you in relation to what happened in Kiseljak, and we suggested that personnel changes be made in the command of the HVO in Kiseljak. And what is attached in the information we saw a few minutes ago --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I am sorry, Ms. Nozica, for interrupting you, but I'm still with the last document, the document, I think it is 6647 or perhaps it's ... I see in the transcript you invoke the document, and then you say you are not going into it and you invoke the next document. Now, what is the purpose of this? Why do you mention it? Why do you use your and our time to go to a document, say this is document so and so, I'm not go into it, and then you go to the next. I just would like to understand?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I kindly ask for a little bit of patience. I think that I know very well what I'm doing. Would you please let me finish, and then you will see why I said that. Just a little bit of patience please. Now we are using more time over this document had I just been allowed to continue, please let me continue and you'll see.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The document that I've just shown you now, the second one, is 6828. In terms of the text of the information, it is identical to the previous document and that's why I didn't want to deal with it. Identical, that's why I didn't want to deal with it. The only difference is that in document 6647, the date is the 13th of November, and in document 6828 as the date when this information was compiled, it says the 23rd --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We can barely hear Ms. Nozica, there are other microphones that are on in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you take part in writing this document? Could you please tell the Trial Chamber when it was compiled? There are two dates for the same document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask for all other microphones that are not being used to be switched off, thank you. We cannot hear the speakers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I authored the majority of what is written here. I did that after returning to Mostar. I actually remember speaking to the head. In view of the situation what was going on in Kiseljak, and around Kiseljak, and in relation to Mr. Rajic, our assessment was that it was necessary to compile a thorough piece of information. So this was written up and then what was added was parts of other reports, and that is how this document came into being. The 23rd of November is the date of this document and that is why these two documents show what they show in this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, shall we take the break now? I believe that the time would be right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. We'll break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bandic, I have received information that I only have ten minutes left, so we will skip over the next document, and I'll just ask you briefly with respect to Ahmici, since this village is mentioned in the previous information, do you know who conducted the investigation in connection with Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, it was the military Prosecutor who conducted the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please look at 4D575. So just skip over one document in your binder. 575. Yes. It says here, this is a document written by Mr. Tihomir Blaskic directly to the commander in chief, Mate Boban, and he says here under 1.2, The Ahmici case is concluded according to your instructions and the video delivered to the chief of the military intelligence service of the Main Staff Zarko Kezo. Did you have information that Mr. Blaskic was authorised by Mr. Boban to conduct this investigation?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours are, I did not have this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Now let's look at the next document, that's P5 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Or, rather, interpreter's correction: P6841.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 6841.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is again information. We are still dealing with Stupni Do, and it's signed by commander of OG group 2, Colonel Rajic. I'll ask you only the following without going further into the contents of this document but looking only at paragraph 1. After receiving a written order from Colonel Tihomir Blaskic, dated the 24th of October, to carry out an investigation against Zlonko Duzinovic, assistant for the information and security service of the Vares brigade. It was determined that this investigation should be carried out by Zoran Duno, assistant for SIS OG 2. Mr. Bandic, please tell Their Honours whether this is in fact the method we discussed earlier respecting the duties of the commander regarding investigations of events which might be misdemeanours or crimes or breaches of discipline, and is this the way these proceedings were conducted as Mr. Rajic did in relation with Mr. Duznovic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the procedure. But, by your leave, it's strange that Mr. Rajic wrote to the president, Mr. Boban, at that time the president of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. It's unusual.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, he's also write to Mr. Blaskic, but what I'm interested in is the following: Why was the he writing this, who was he at the time, and what was the connection between Mr. Rajic and Ante Sliskovic, the assistant commander for Vitez or, rather, the Vitez military district?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's evident from this that Mr. Rajic was addressing the persons he needed to address. It was -- Colonel Blaskic was the commander of the military district, and then there was Mr. Sliskovic. And in this letter we can see that Zoran Duno was designated, his assistant, Mr. Rajic's assistant for OG 2 was designated to carry out the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now that we are dealing with Mr. Duznovic, please look at 2D942. This is a report - and we saw from the previous document - that Mr. Duznovic, against whom the investigation was being conducted, and we can see in this document dated the 23rd of February, 1994, that this document is a report according to which Mr. Zvonko Duznovic was found dead. Did you have information about these events concerning Mr. Zvonko Duznovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Bandic. I object to this line of questioning. It's irrelevant and it's beyond the scope of the witness summaries that have been provided in respect of this witness, this issue regarding Mr. Duznovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, what is the relevance of this?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the relevance is in that we are showing how because of the previous documents and the witness statement of EA, here in the courtroom as I stated before, we see an example here as to how an investigation was conducted and how in this particular case it was ordered by (redacted), and I think it's quite significant. This can be compared with his statements, as we have already said in the transcript of 24541 to 24862, when he said that in the case of Stupni Do, the investigation was to be conducted by this witness together with his assistant for SIS, Mr. Duno, and it's evident from the previous document that (redacted) issued an order to Mr. Duno telling him to carry out this investigation. So he acted differently from what he said before this court regarding this witness. Mr. Dunic [as interpreted] is connected with events in Stupni Do in a number of documents. I don't think this had to be stressed particularly, but this is a document which deals very briefly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'll just ask you the following: Do you know something about these events?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, I'm familiar with this event and unfortunately Mr. Duzinovic's death. His name is Duzinovic, not Duznovic. I knew him personally, and I know that proceedings were initiated against certain persons because of this murder. And please excuse me, but let me mention, it's relevant because Mr. Duznovic was SIS's man in the brigade, Bobovac-Vares.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bandic, in connection with Mr. Duznovic's death, I'm reading it out as it's written in the document, if it's misprinted in the document, thank you for the correction. Please tell me the following: We talked about your method of work and how operatives worked, how the people in the brigades were in charge of SIS worked, so could you tell Their Honours according to the information you have, with the exception of Mr. Duzinovic were there also other cases of murders or unsolved murders and other cases concerning people working in SIS?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Objection. It's irrelevant and it's beyond the scope of the witness summary that's been provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer, I believe that this could be interesting. I can't say why. I'd rather listen to the answers. Ms. Nozica, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you for saying what you did. I think it's very important because we are talking about the conditions and circumstances prevailing at the time and the witness did say that their job was highly unpopular, and I think it's very important to assess the conditions under which people did their work, so I think that this question is important.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could the witness tell us how many persons died or were killed or were -- well, how many persons were killed primarily, and whether these cases were solved, and where these people did their work?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, these are two glaring examples in the Kiseljak area. One was the murder of Mr. Duznovic of the SIS of the Bobovac Brigade from Vares, and the second case was a brutal murder of a SIS member in Kiseljak. His name was Mr. Lujo -- or, rather, Zeljko Bosnjak, also known as Lujo. Two other men were killed together with him, and the status of the other person who was murdered was unclear to me, but Mr. Bosnjak was a member of the SIS. When I arrived on the ground in Kiseljak, I found him there as one of the persons who were in the HVO SIS and he was killed. I think in the summer of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Tell me, did SIS conduct any investigations concerning these murders, and did they submit this material to the Prosecutor's Office; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the details, but I know that proceedings were initiated in connection with these murders.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now we'll move on to my last topic, Mr. Bandic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Just one question which perhaps is not entirely relevant, but in the previous document, P06841, at the end we read that the president, Mate Boban, had requested the transfer of, inter alia, one Zvonko Duznovic, to him to Grude. And as it is the same name, I wonder whether he is the one identical with the one who was later murdered? Can you verbalize the answer because otherwise your nodding is not recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you are right. Mr. Boban's intervention concerned several people to be transferred to Herzegovina for their protection because they were being detained in Kiseljak pursuant to a decision issued by Mr. Rajic, but unfortunately, Mr. Duznovic did not survive to be transferred because he was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: So there was on 23rd November, 1993, that Supreme Commander, Mate Boban, requested the urgent transfer of Zvonko Duznovic who was murdered on 22 February, 1994, that is three months later. Is that -- can we -- what do we have to conclude on the authority of orders by Mate Boban, if we look at this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, many things were illogical in that time and in that place. The authority of Mr. Boban was unchallenged; although, towards the end of 1993, it was already considerably weakened and his replacement was also being discussed. Mr. Duznovic was there throughout this time and unfortunately he was killed as is stated here, in February 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 1994, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We'll now look at a similar document, that's P3988, dated the 6th of August. We have no signature here, but we see it's a report by the prison warden of that date, and it was received on the 18th of August, 1993 by the SIS in Mostar, and the last document --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, for the intervention. I'm being told that these last two exhibits are confidential.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, thank you. I omitted to do this. These are documents 3906 and 3988. If we can agree, I won't read out the contents and we don't have to show them in e-court. I'm only interested in the dates on these documents so they need not be seen outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And the last document bears a date, it's 4177, that's the document number. P4177. The document was signed by Mr. Luka Markesic, and the date is the 14th of August, 1993, and it was received in the Mostar SIS on 18th of August, 1993. Mr. Bandic, do you have any information as to why these documents were received in the Mostar SIS, one on the 17th of August, 1993, two on the 18th of August, 1993, although they were all compiled quite sometime before those dates?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, Your Honours, I know the answer in part. I know part of the reason, I'm not familiar with the details of course. I think that that was when I was on the ground in central Bosnia, but I remember that this was an important case. It was a high-profile case. There were conflicts at the level of the operative zone and the brigade in Rama regarding the SIS, and he personally went up there to resolve the situation to see what was going on. And after that, he withdrew Mr. Markesic from his post as assistant for SIS in the brigade. I think that for awhile Mr. Markesic was on leave, and then an attempt was made to establish a centre in Rama, and Mr. Markesic was appointed to it. The reason the documents arrived when they did is, I assume, that Mr. Markesic gave them to Mr. Lucic personally, and Mr. Lucic took them to Mostar with him. Or perhaps they were sent to Mostar, which I think is the reason why the dates are more or less the same, whereas the documents were compiled two or three weeks prior to that, but the dates are the same as to the time of when they were received. So this has to do with the brigade SIS and the SIS of the military district.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the last two documents. 2D1506. It is a document from which we can see that on the 25th of August, after these documents had been received and after the meeting, as you said, with Mr. Lucic, that Mr. Markesic is replaced and discharged from the duty to assume another duty. And then the next document, 2D1505. 1505, dated the same day, a decision whereby Mr. Luka Markesic is appointed to the duty of -- in the SIS centre, to the position of head of SIS centre Rama. Is this what you discussed, Mr. Bandic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is exactly what was going on. I personally knew Mr. Markesic during the war, and this was a sort of a recognition of his work in that particular case. The head of the administration judged him to be right. He withdrew him from the brigade and at his proposal, Mr. Bruno Stojic, head of the Defence Department, appointed him as head of the SIS centre Rama, but unfortunately that centre never functioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: My last question, Mr. Bandic. Have you ever head of Mr. Mate Zadro being an employee of SIS administration, that he withdrew his salary from the SIS administration? Have you ever heard of anything like that? We've seen the lists, the payroll lists, but do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of that. Usually, people who were connected in any way at centre level or administration level, I knew them almost personally, almost all of them, but I do not know Mr. Zadro and I'm not aware of any of his connections with the SIS.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question -- last question referred to page 10434 concerning the statement of the witness under the pseudonym of CC. My questions have been exhausted. Mr. Bandic, thank you for answering them. Your Honours, my examination-in-chief hereby concludes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to organise myself. Your Honours, I'd like to greet you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Greet you, Mr. Bandic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And greet everybody in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: As I said yesterday on one occasion, Mr. Bandic, we had occasion to meet two, two and a half or three years ago. We conducted conversations over the telephone. I would like you to ask you to confirm to the Bench whether this is correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. But it's not completely fleshed out with all the details that we discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: No need to go into details. I did not take part in proofing you for this testimony, and neither I nor anybody else from Mr. Petkovic Defence?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, but we did discuss for my possible appearance here as a witness for the Defence Mr. Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes, three and a half years ago I talked to you as a person that may have some knowledge about events concerning the indictment; isn't that correct? After that one meeting and conversation, we have never met in the meantime; is that correct? First of all, Mr. Bandic, I'm going to ask you about one of the last questions of Mr. Bruno Stojic's Defence team. You mentioned how Mr. Zeljko Bosnjak and Mr. Duznovic were murdered, about the difficult circumstances in which SIS personnel worked. I would like you to tell the Chamber whether a claim is true, and that claim is contained in P6828. This is one of the reports that we discussed as documents of almost identical content, the operative combination of Kiseljak. There's no need for us to -- reading that document. I'm going to read out a section concerning Mr. Bosnjak and since you are an author of part of that information, I would like you to confirm whether this is true. Whether it's true that Mr. Bosnjak involved in illegal activities and that he associated with antisocial persons who followed his conduct, conflict with Mr. Rajic culminated in August this year when Mr. Rajic engaged some of his people and liquidated Bosnjak and his cup-bearers; Mr. Petsurepa [phoen], aka Legija; and Ivica Petsurepa, aka Pezar [phoen]. Could you tell us whether this is true?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which report you are referring to, but the facts are true.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The report is one of those documents which have identical contents of which you admitted authorship. Is this true concerning Mr. Bosnjak?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have this document in front of me, so this is why I say that I don't know which document you are talking about, but the information that you quoted is true, that such information was gathered in connection with this event and those persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, whether SIS had any information about Mr. Duznovic being involved in illegal actives in the area of Vares?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally have no knowledge about that. But I presume that, and this is what SIS does and Mr. Duznovic was an SIS operative, I don't know whether he had engaged in any criminal activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Fine. Now, Mr. Bandic, let's clarify some details concerning your positions, your functions. I hope that we will be quick about it. In listing the positions at the beginning of your testimony, you confirmed a question of Mr. Stojic's Defence that from the end of 1992 to 1994, you were in SIS administration; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct completely. I was not in the administration from April because it was established in July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So it's reflected so in the transcript, that's incorrect?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Because between April and July I was in military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Fine. Could you tell us whether from October 1992 and autumn 1994 you were part of the SIS administration?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That can be said in this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Soon afterwards you said that in -- from summer 1993 you were at the Main Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date believe me, but somewhere around that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you explain please, for us, that at the same time that you were in the SIS administration and the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simple, I did not have a document appointing me there, but because of the nature of my work and constant company of Mr. Petkovic, I physically was located at the Main Staff for awhile. I'm not sure whether I ever received appointment decree to work at the SIS administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: With respect to the documents, were you an SIS personnel at the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So that you're not an employee of the SIS administration in the SIS administration at the same time?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't preclude, this is not mutually preclusive.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Fine. You told us that you were in the escort of Mr. Petkovic, General Petkovic, on his visits to central Bosnia and Sarajevo; is that correct? Could you please repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Please tell us, did you follow Mr. Petkovic when he travelled to Split, Geneva, or other places?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Mainly these were visits to central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Please tell us, if you were detailed to work at the Main Staff and you were supposed to escort General Petkovic, how is it that you escorted him only when he visited central Bosnia and Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's only logical in my opinion, Mr. Petkovic, General Petkovic attending peace negotiations outside Bosnia-Herzegovina because these were political and military negotiations, and in my capacity I could not have been involved in those. And when he visited central Bosnia, as I stated earlier, on top of by virtue of the nature of my job, I was seconded to Mr. Petkovic as an assistant.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bandic, did your operative work as SIS operative, did include the area of central Bosnia and Sarajevo, or did your work include some other areas?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no limitations. It was the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina; wherever HVO forces were, this was part of my area of responsibility. This was not exclusively restricted to central Bosnia. I personally, for instance, never went to Posavina.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Apart from central Bosnia, where else did you work as an SIS officer elsewhere in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the other areas. I visited the area of Tomislavgrad, Livno, south-east Herzegovina, central Bosnia, there where HVO forces were stationed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a look at the first set of my documents. Let's go through them quickly. Some of them are known to you. The first one is 2D003939 [as interpreted]. 939, 2D939. This is a payroll list of Security Sector employees for July 1993. You are referred to under item 2, Mr. Ivan Bandic. Would it be logical to conclude that in July 1993 you received a salary as an employee in the Security Sector of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's logical.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Fine. Let's take a look at the next document, P5467. This is Mr. Bruno Stojic's proposal to Mr. Gojko Susak, recommending a promotion of HVO officers for a comission with the Croatian military and suggestion that Mr. Bandic, who is a major brigadier in HVO and proposed to assume the rank of major in the HV. Does this refer to you Mr. Bandic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Would it be logical to infer that the end of September you were head of the administrative department of the SIS in the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I would like to supplement this with the following: Since you've noticed that at different situations I'm introduced by different titles. Sometimes assistant head or chief or head of administrative department. Believe me, I personally don't know all the titles that were attached to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at another document, 2D942. 2D942. It is a report that SIS assistant commander of the Kiseljak Brigade sends to you, to the SIS administration in Mostar. My question is, were you at the time of this report being submitted, that's February, 1994, whether you were a member of the SIS administration at Mostar?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. At that time, yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Fine. Given your statement that you were at the Main Staff, please take a look at the next document, 4D1311. It is an Article by Mr. Ivica Lucic entitled "Security and Intelligence Services in Bosnia-Herzegovina." On page 9, somewhere down the middle of the page in the English version that would be the first quarter of the second large paragraph that was translated, I'm interested in one statement by Mr. Ivica Lucic, where he says that there were no SIS personnel at the Main Staff. Could you tell us whether this statement is true or untrue?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot find the article. I don't think that this is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Fine. Let's take a look at the next document. 4D1652. That's your interview to Globus magazine dated the 2nd of December, 2005. After the content of Mr. Ivica Rajic had been --

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is only the title page.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Impossible.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In that article, you say at the end of the first column, beginning of the second column, the author introduces you as a person who, during the conflict with the Muslims, was sent to central Bosnia as a formal liaison officer with the -- for the Main Staff of the HVO who informs on the events of Kiseljak, Vares, Zepca, in Usora, then sends information to the Main Staff. Is it true that you had some tasks, intelligent tasks in central Bosnia and that you were formally labelled as a person who has connections with the Main Staff because it would be inappropriate for you to introduce yourself as an intelligence officer whenever you had contacts with UNPROFOR representatives or whoever else you got in contact with?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reiterate, for a time I was in the SIS administration. For a time I was at the Main Staff, and of course this was not determined officially when I would be in the administration, when I would be in the Main Staff. My task was for somebody of -- who has experience to be of assistance to HVO commanders, in this case to Mr. Petkovic, whenever we went out into the field in central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, let's take a look at the next document. P03177. It is an official note compiled by crime investigation officer, Stefan Petric, on an interview with you dated 3rd of July, 2000, in the premises of Croatian MUP. First of all, have you ever seen this document?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And did you talk to a MUP official of the Republic of Croatia in mid-2000?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Please look at page 2, the first paragraph, it says: "In September 1992, the said person was sent to the area of central Bosnia with a view to collect information that is of security interest, and the cover for his work was the position of assistant head of the Main Staff for security within which he was in charge of the security of General Milivoj Petkovic. He remained in central Bosnia in this way all the way up to the signing of the accords in 1994." Mr. Bandic, my question is whether it is true that you said that you had your own independent tasks in central Bosnia and that Milivoj Petkovic was just a cover for your activities?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, since we are talking about a document that has to do with the time while I was still a member of the Croatian service, I cannot speak about that unless I get permission from the authorities of the republic of Croatia.
